answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via global max-flow checks on a bonded vouching graph. Each agent is a vertex needing a fixed flow quota from a vetted trust anchor along stake-backed edges. Because flow conservation caps aggregate flow across any cut, one bridge cannot harbor extra fake accounts, forcing attackers to lock slashable capital per identity. However, correlated slashing risk can deter honest participants from vouching for legitimate newcomers.
